description:
Fold MA-13 — the second blocker on KMI count (i), and the half that genuinely is KMI's own work. MA-12's carrier belongs on KCB §4; this one moves no clause outside KMI.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored). The break is real and it is structural:

- §7.1(e) bullet 2 is written over the asset: 'Where an ASSET'S `egress` is `local-only`, it MUST NOT be replicated across an authority-domain boundary and no holder may serve it across one, irrespective of that holder's own policy.'
- But §2 makes the pair a PER-ASSERTER ENVELOPE FIELD: `license` and `egress` are 'envelope fields, so they are asserted by whoever asserted the envelope and are read off its `prov` — never off the store that served the bytes (§7.1(d))', and both are 'excluded from the id like every other field here'.
- And the `asset` id binds BYTES: §7.1(a) — 'the `asset` id *is* the hash of the bytes, so the same bytes carry the same id in every store'.
- So TWO CONFORMANT ENVELOPES FOR ONE ID MAY DISAGREE, and nothing ranks them. §7.1(d) sources the travelling pair from 'the envelope the REQUESTING participant already holds', so a holder with only the permissive copy satisfies bullet 1 (it evaluated the asset's own pair), breaches bullet 2 (the asset's `egress` is `local-only` somewhere it cannot see), and CANNOT DISCOVER the pair that would have stopped it — (d) forbids synthesizing an envelope, and no verb hands it a second one.
- NO MISBEHAVIOUR AT ANY HOP. That is why §2's attribution answer does not reach it: attribution says whose assertion a pair is, and the question here is which of two honest assertions governs.

THE FOLD — KMI-ONLY, ADDITIVE, MINTING NO FIELD. Three edits, each held to what the break forces:
(a) §7.1(d) names the SERVING participant's evaluated pair as the one that travels, closing the gap (d) opens by sourcing it from the requester's copy;
(b) §7.1(e) states that where a holder has more than one conformant pair the MOST RESTRICTIVE GOVERNS, and a holder MUST NOT prefer its own — ADR-0013's monotone-restrictive discipline reused, exactly as ADR-0014 reuses it, and exactly as KFT §4.2 already takes the most restrictive `egress` across a job's inputs;
(c) (e) bullet 2's MUST is scoped to the pairs a holder HOLDS OR HAS RECEIVED, leaving the fail-closed default for ABSENCE unchanged — §7.1(e)'s existing rule that a holder without the governing policy MUST NOT serve onward across a boundary, and MUST NOT synthesize the missing pair to pass the gate, is untouched.

WHAT DOES NOT MOVE. No `asset` id moves, no envelope field is added, no KGP clause moves (KGP §7.2 still filters `local-only` RECORDS at pack construction; these fields govern BYTES and are evaluated by the serving participant at `fetch` time), and DEFER-C is unmoved.

THEN RE-RUN STEPS 8-10 — WITH MA-12, which the same re-run must clear. That is why this depends on `920`: a Steps 8-10 walk that clears only one of the two blockers cannot close count (i), and walking it twice against half-folded text buys nothing.

userStories.title: §7.1(d) — the serving participant's evaluated pair is the one that travels
userStories.description: Close the sourcing gap. (d) today takes the travelling pair from the envelope the REQUESTING participant holds, which is how a permissive copy reaches a holder that will then serve under it.
acceptanceCriteria: §7.1(d) names the SERVING participant's evaluated pair as the one that travels with a replicated copy, replacing the current sourcing from the requesting participant's copy, with the reason stated in the text.

The narrow-exception framing of (d) is preserved: the `license`/`egress` pair remains the SINGLE thing permitted to accompany a replication besides the bytes, precisely because it is not synthesized. No envelope is fabricated, no lineage edge is written, no `prov` record is minted.
No field is minted and no `asset` id moves. Verified against §2's field list and §7.1(a), not assumed.

GATES: `node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs`, `node scripts/check-registry.mjs`, `node scripts/check-tasklist-categories.mjs` and `bash scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh` all green, with the observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: §7.1(d)'s travels-with-the-bytes carve-out now names the SERVING participant's pair as evaluated under (e) as the one that travels, replacing the sourcing from the requesting participant's copy, with the reason in the text (the server must evaluate before serving, so the value exists at the serve; the requester may hold no envelope at all). Narrow-exception framing preserved verbatim in substance — still the single thing permitted alongside the bytes, still a carry and not a synthesis, no envelope fabricated / no lineage edge / no `prov` minted. No field minted and no `asset` id moves, VERIFIED by diff not assumption: §2 byte-unchanged, §7.1(a)–(c) byte-unchanged, §7.1(e)–(f) and the tail byte-unchanged. Also fixed a pre-existing doc-integrity break inherited from 920's retire (promotability.md pointed at tasks/chief/920-….json, moved to completed/). userStories.title: §7.1(e) — the most restrictive pair governs, and absence still fails closed
userStories.description: The ranking rule the break asked for, plus the scoping that keeps it from disturbing what already works.
acceptanceCriteria: §7.1(e) states that where a holder has MORE THAN ONE conformant `license`/`egress` pair for one `asset` id, the MOST RESTRICTIVE governs, and a holder MUST NOT prefer its own. The clause cites ADR-0013's monotone-restrictive discipline as reused — naming that KFT §4.2 already takes the most restrictive `egress` across a job's inputs, so this is one rule applied again rather than a second convention invented.

(e) bullet 2's MUST is scoped to the pairs a holder HOLDS OR HAS RECEIVED. The existing fail-closed default for ABSENCE is unchanged and said to be unchanged: a holder with bytes and no governing policy MUST NOT serve them onward across an authority-domain boundary, MAY still serve them inside its own domain, and MUST NOT synthesize the missing pair to pass the gate.

No KGP clause moves and no KGP enforcement point moves — KGP §7.2 still filters `local-only` records at pack construction; these fields govern bytes and are evaluated by the serving participant at `fetch` time. Checked against the text of KGP §7.1/§7.2, not asserted.
DEFER-C is explicitly unmoved, and a disposition for MA-13 is recorded alongside the existing MA dispositions, reasoning the fold's extent.

The KMI version move is decided under KMI's own rules and recorded with reasoning; if it moves, all three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it, and KMI's declared removal of `application/vnd.koine.edl+json` at KMI 0.4.0 is checked rather than tripped.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: KMI 0.3.7 -> 0.3.8 (patch). §7.1(e) gains the divergence rule: where a holder has MORE THAN ONE conformant license/egress pair for one asset id, the MOST RESTRICTIVE governs, taken PER AXIS (narrowest license class; local-only over exportable), and a holder MUST NOT prefer its own pair NOR the pair that permits the serve. Cited as ADR-0013's monotone-restrictive discipline REUSED — naming ADR-0014's federated merge and KFT §4.2's most-restrictive egress across a job's inputs (verified in specs/fine-tuning.md:695) — plus the measured asymmetry (a restriction taken in error costs a refused serve, recoverable; one missed is bytes across a boundary, which nothing undoes). (e) bullet 2's MUST rewritten and SCOPED to the pairs a holder HOLDS OR HAS RECEIVED, with 'an obligation to act on what a holder knows, never a duty to discover what it does not'. Absence default UNCHANGED and said to be unchanged: bullet 3 is byte-unchanged (verified by diff — the only removed lines in the whole spec are the version line and bullet 2's two lines) and the new text restates it explicitly (MUST NOT serve onward across a boundary, MAY serve inside its own domain, MUST NOT synthesize). NO KGP CLAUSE MOVES — checked against the text, not asserted: read KGP §7.1 (records carry an SPDX license, admitted per record at the consumer) and §7.2 ('the filter is applied at pack construction'); both are about RECORDS, neither mentions bytes or a serving holder, and grounding-pack.md is untouched in this diff. DEFER-C explicitly unmoved in the 0.3.8 status note, the §7.1 count paragraph, the changelog, the MA-13 disposition row and CLAUDE.md; its trigger row in federation-fold-dispositions.md is byte-unchanged. MA-13's disposition recorded beside MA-1…MA-12 in docs/reference/federation-fold-dispositions.md (new section, title updated), reasoning extent: the break forces a RANKING and not a registry of pairs / canonical asserter / signature / discovery verb, each of which answers 'whose pair is authoritative' rather than 'which honest pair governs'. VERSION MOVE DECIDED UNDER KMI'S OWN RULES and recorded: patch, because no field/enum/envelope is minted, every surface is additive, a holder that only ever sees one pair behaves exactly as at 0.3.7 — and because 0.4.0 IS SPENT on §4.4's EDL removal (CHECKED, not tripped: §4.4's declared removal version is untouched and KCB §7.3c forbids declaring and removing in one publication). All three mirrors moved (README.md:62, specs/README.md:16, ECOSYSTEM.md:47) plus the un-gated prose list at specs/README.md:288 and CLAUDE.md's Current state. Additivity proven by SECTION SLICE against HEAD, not eyeballed: §1, §2, §3, §4, §5, §6, §8, §9 and Pressure test all 'SAME'; only §7, Changelog and the header differ.
